trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going up would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,1). So the line goes down.
Going left would leave both cell (4,1) and number 3 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Going right would leave both number 9 and cell (6,4) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going right would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going down would force the line onto number 6 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (2,2) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going up would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes right.
Going up leaves no safe move afterwards; going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
The line must go down: up is number 11, which comes later.
Cell (4,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (5,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going down would wall in number 11, the last number. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
